title: Normalized rational localization triangles and cross-object orthogonality
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $T=X,U,Z$ use the derived-complete integral category $\mathcal C_T=D^b_c(T,R)$ and its raw rationalization $\mathcal C_T[1/t]=D^b_c(T,E)$, with no Karoubi completion [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $Q_T$ for the identity-on-objects localization functor, with $\operatorname{Hom}(Q_TK,Q_TL)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)\otimes_RE$.

The actual rational functors $i^*,j^*,i_*,j_!$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], [def-weil-derived-direct-image], [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] are exact $E$-linear functors obtained by rationalizing their integral counterparts. The adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $i^*\dashv i_*$ rationalize as adjunctions, including their specified units and counits, for every rational morphism, without requiring an integral representative of that morphism. In particular, the open counit $\varepsilon^E$ and closed unit $\eta^E$ have components $Q_X(\varepsilon^R_K)$ and $Q_X(\eta^R_K)$.

For every integral $K\in\mathcal C_X$ and every distinguished integral completion
$$j_!j^*K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon^R_K}K\xrightarrow{\eta^R_K}i_*i^*K\xrightarrow{\delta}j_!j^*K[1],$$
its image under $Q_X$, with the canonical shift comparison, is a distinguished triangle with the rational counit and unit. For arbitrary $N\in D^b_c(U,E)$, $M\in D^b_c(Z,E)$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, writing $\widetilde N,\widetilde M$ for the same objects in the integral categories, the canonical identification is
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,E)}(j_!N[m],i_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_c(X,R)}(j_!\widetilde N[m],i_*\widetilde M)\otimes_RE=0.$$
These identifications use the normalized operations and adjunction maps, not alternative functors with merely isomorphic vertices.

proof.text: Apply integralSupportFunctorNormalization to obtain the inherited geometry, specified integral support functors, exact linear shifts, open adjunction and disjointness. The adjoint shifts give exact linear integral pullbacks. Reduction is fully faithful on complete objects, by its invertible reconstruction unit. Compose the reduction Hom equivalence, the normalized pullback/reduction isomorphism, the system pullback/direct-image adjunction, and reduction/total-limit adjunction to construct the closed integral adjunction. Evaluating its unit at the identity gives the required whole-system closed-unit equation. The open counit equation follows from openSystemCounit by naturality of the reduction/limit counit.

Use the specified additive rational pullbacks and compact-support tensor action. Construct the closed rational image by the semilinear extension for the identity coefficient map. All four functors satisfy Q Fq = F Q by their pure tensor formulas. Raw Q is a categorical localization: compare its tensor Hom modules with Rationalization.tensorHomEquiv, obtaining a fully faithful essentially surjective comparison. Descend the integral shift comparisons using Functor.commShiftOfLocalization. Naturality of the factorization equality supplies the shift equation in every integer degree. The torsion-cone denominators admit left fractions, so localization is essentially surjective on arrows. Mathlib isTriangulated_of_precomp descends exactness of each extended functor, and tensor induction proves coefficient-field linearity on all rational arrows.

Apply Mathlib Adjunction.localization to the two specified integral adjunctions and the literal functor factorization equalities. Its unit and counit component formulas are the integral maps tensored with one, up to transports along those equalities, which give the required HEq statements. The construction is natural on all localized arrows.

Apply the exact localization Q to every given integral distinguished completion. Transport its three vertices along the literal object formulas of the rational operations. The localized unit and counit HEq equations fix its first two arrows; equality transport retains the last arrow Q(delta) followed by the specified Q shift comparison.

For arbitrary independent integral N,M and any integer m, precompose with the shift comparison J(N[m]) isomorphic to J(N)[m] and use the open adjunction. Disjointness makes the resulting target P(I(M)) zero, so the integral cross Hom is a subsingleton. Tensoring a subsingleton module gives a subsingleton. Transport the rational Hom along the object equalities and Q shift isomorphism to its scalar-first tensor Hom, also a subsingleton. The unique additive equivalence of the two zero groups satisfies the prescribed pure-tensor coordinate equation.
